marks.gloss_en: מה לבעל מום שכן עשה בו קריבין כמקריבין -- with blemishes the Torah equated disqualified ANIMALS with disqualified officiants, a stringency aninut lacks
זר יוכיח -- the non-priest has no sacrifice-equals-officiant stringency, yet his service desecrates
לא ראי זה כראי זה: the common element of the blemished priest and the non-priest -- they are warned off the service, and if they served they desecrated -- brings in the onen, who is warned
the ordinary priest is WARNED against serving as onen -- the premise the tzad hashaveh's common element needs
מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן לא הותרה מכללו -- neither source's prohibition is EVER permitted, whereas aninut is permitted from its rule for the High Priest
טמא יוכיח -- impurity IS permitted from its rule (for communal offerings), yet the impure priest desecrates
הצד השוה שבהן שמוזהרין ואם עבדו חיללו -- the common element of the impure, the blemished and the non-priest brings in the onen

ולפרוך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן לא הותרו מכללן אצל כהן גדול בקרבן יחיד -- none of the three is permitted even to a High Priest for an individual offering, whereas the onen High Priest serves even individual offerings

שם טומאה מיהא אישתראי -- the CATEGORY of impurity is at least permitted (for communal offerings), so the three do not share the claimed no-exception stringency; the objection is deflected and the schema stands
if the seated priest, who may eat of offerings, desecrates the service if he served seated, then the onen, who may not eat, all the more so
מה ליושב שכן פסול לעדות -- one who sits is disqualified from testifying, a stringency the onen lacks
מיושב תלמיד חכם -- derive instead from the seated Torah scholar, who IS fit to testify seated, yet desecrates the service if he served seated
היכן מוזהר? אילימא מומן המקדש לא יצא -- חילול בגופיה כתיב ביה! -- if the warning is that verse, desecration is written outright and the kal vachomer is unnecessary
אלא מהן הקריבו -- וקסבר מפני אנינות נשרפה: the warning premise rides on R' Elazar's source, read as an aninut consequence
the sin-offering was burned because Aaron and his sons were acute mourners -- the reading הן הקריבו requires, held by R' Elazar and by the tanna of the kal vachomer

the fallback: even if the shem-yoshev pircha does refute, the law is derived from the seated scholar together with ANY ONE of those three (zar / tamei / baal mum) -- a conditional derivation with a disjunctive second source; no schema construct can state either feature, so it is recorded here as a proposition
